title: Запертые в холодильнике  (Locked in the Walk-in Fridge)

segments.t: Once Nastya is inside the cold room, Kostya lures Sasha in after her by pretending he lost his phone among the shelves, and the boys bolt the door shut. Instead of making peace, however, Sasha and Nastya realize Max set them up and immediately start trading insults.
Настя, я в холодильнике свой телефон потерял.
Наверное, все Макс твой придумал, да?
Now let's break down each line of their conversation.
'Did I understand that correctly?' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'I' and finishing on 'understood?'. Kostya answers right away.
'Will I be able to come visit?' The meaning hinges on 'and' working together with 'to come' in spoken Russian.
'All right, fine.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'come on' before landing on 'really?!'.
'Come on, call my phone for me, will you?' Max raises the pitch on 'and' to turn the phrase into a direct spoken question. Kostya answers right away.
Настя, я в холодильнике свой телефон потерял.
'Nastya, I lost my phone in the walk-in fridge.' The grammar packs 'Nastya' and 'lost' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
'What were you doing in the walk-in fridge?' The '-l' ending on the verb meaning 'were doing' places the action in the masculine past tense.
'Nastya, go make some juice.' The meaning hinges on 'Nastya' working together with 'what is one to do' in spoken Russian. Kostya answers right away.
'Well, that is it.' Notice how Russian expresses 'come on' and 'all' with crisp inflection rather than helper words.
Наверное, все Макс твой придумал, да?
'Your Max probably came up with all of this, right?' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'probably' before landing on 'yes'.
'Of course it was Max.' In Russian, the idea of 'of course' flows naturally into 'Max' without extra filler words. Kostya answers right away.
'Watch your mouth, you sheep.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'behind' before landing on 'sheep'.
'Be quiet right now, dwarf.' Notice how Russian puts 'to be quiet' and 'dwarf' together in a short, direct phrase where word endings show how the ideas connect.

'They are probably hugging each other already.' Here Max anchors the thought on 'probably' and finishes on 'to hug each other, to embrace', keeping the spoken rhythm brisk and natural. Now let's put it all back together and hear the whole scene again.
Настя, я в холодильнике свой телефон потерял.
Наверное, все Макс твой придумал, да?

That wraps up this scene as max and Kostya trick both Nastya and Sasha into stepping inside the walk-in refrigerator and lock the door, only for the two girls to immediately start insulting each other. See you next time!
